newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 15.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 15.6 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 15.6 percent of its average daily volume of 351.6 million shares, or 54.8 million shares, for the week of Sept. 3-6.
Program trading accounted for an average of 14.1 percent of average daily volume of 293.4 million shares for the week of August 26-30.
Of the average 54.8 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 19.8 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 35.0 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 70.1 million shares a day during the week of Sept. 3-6.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, Nomura Securities, Morgan Stanley, First Boston and Lehman Brothers executed most of their program activity for their own accounts. First Options executed most of its program activity for customers, as agent.

In aggregate, program volume executed on the NYSE by firms as agents, for non-member customers, amounted to 52.0 percent during Sept. 3-6. Program volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 46.5 percent of program volume.
During Sept. 3-6, 31.8 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms related to index arbitrage.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
